newsitem.title: USA: Weld to resign as governor to focus on envoy bid.
newsitem.headline: Weld to resign as governor to focus on envoy bid.

text.p: Republican William Weld will resign as governor of Massachusetts Monday to work full-time for Senate confirmation to be U.S. ambassador to Mexico, a White House official said Sunday.

The official, who asked not to be identified, said Weld had communicated his decision to White House Chief of Staff Erskine Bowles and that Bowles had informed President Clinton, who is midway through a three-day trip through the U.S. West. Weld was to make the announcement Monday in Boston, the official said.

"Governor Weld has been a skilled leader and we continue to believe he will make an excellent ambassador to Mexico," White House spokesman Joe Lockhart told reporters when asked about Weld's reported decison to resign as governor.
Jesse Helms, the North Carolina Republican who heads the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, has vowed to block any Senate vote on Weld, whom he deems too soft on drugs for Mexico.
Weld has supported the medical use of marijuana and taken abortion and gay rights stances that are anathema to Helms, who has said the governor was below "ambassador quality."
The official said Weld made his decision to resign on his own, and did not consult the White House on it.
